newsitem.title: ISRAEL: CPI not seen influencing Israeli share market.
newsitem.headline: CPI not seen influencing Israeli share market.

text.p: The Israeli share market greeted the November consumer price index warmly, but traders said on Sunday the market would be more influenced by other factors.
"For several weeks the market was focused on macro issues and the budget and now on the political situation," said Gad Haker of Betucha Securities and Investments. "The index was no big event today."
The Central Bureau of Statistics said Israel consumer prices in November rose 0.6 percent, following a 0.8 percent rise month-on-month in October.

"The index was exactly according to forecasts and expectations are now for a symbolic interest rate cut of up to 0.5 percentage point this month," said Zvi Hoffman of Meiatv Investments and Securities, adding: "This is conditional on there being no new delays in approval of the budget."

The Treasury is now awaiting line item cuts on the 1997 budget from the ministries before going back to parliament with a second round of budget cuts of 1.2 billion shekels. The total spending cut is expected to be 6.1 billion shekels, and parliament has until December 31 to approve it.
Haker said with inflationary expectations in the bond market now at about 9.6 percent, real interest rates are approximately 5.6 percent. "It's way too much," he said.

The base short-term rate is currently 15.2 percent, where it has been since the end of October. The Bank of Israel is due to announce its January monetary programme, which includes rates, on December 23.
